question: Why is waste considered more than just inert rubbish in healthcare settings?

options.A: It takes up too much physical space in hospitals
options.B: It acts as a dynamic reservoir of infectious microbial populations
options.C: It is always chemically reactive and unstable
options.D: It smells unpleasant to patients and staff

explanation: Healthcare waste harbors diverse pathogens like bacteria and viruses that can multiply rapidly on organic matter, making it an infectious reservoir rather than just inert rubbish. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is a key objective of proper waste management in relation to microbiology?

options.A: Increasing the rate of microbial reproduction
options.B: Enhancing the aesthetic appeal of hospital grounds
options.C: Breaking the chain of infection by containing pathogens
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital administrative supplies

explanation: Proper containment and disposal break the chain of infection, protecting patients, staff, and the community from healthcare-associated infections. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following best describes general healthcare waste?

options.C: Paper, cardboard, and food leftovers from non-isolated areas
options.D: Human tissues and amputated body parts

explanation: General waste resembles household refuse like paper and food scraps that do not pose special biological hazards. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h2)

question: Why is accurate classification of healthcare waste essential?

options.A: It ensures hazardous waste is treated safely without treating all waste as hazardous
options.B: It allows hospitals to eliminate waste management costs entirely
options.C: It guarantees that all waste can be recycled into domestic goods
options.D: It prevents the generation of municipal garbage

explanation: Proper classification balances safety and cost, ensuring high-risk hazardous materials are managed strictly while avoiding expensive special treatment for safe general refuse. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h2)

question: What is a primary danger associated with improperly disposed sharps?

options.A: Contamination of local groundwater with heavy metals
options.B: Direct inoculation of blood-borne pathogens into the bloodstream
options.C: Attraction of stray animals to hospital premises
options.D: Foul odors affecting patient recovery in wards

explanation: Improperly disposed sharps can cause needlestick injuries, directly inoculating blood-borne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis into the bloodstream. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h3)

question: How do disease vectors contribute to microbiological risks from poor waste disposal?

options.A: They neutralize harmful bacteria in the soil
options.B: They mechanically transfer pathogens from waste to food and water supplies
options.D: They act as natural incinerators for infectious waste

explanation: Vectors like flies and rodents feed on unsecured waste and mechanically transfer pathogens to food and water, causing disease outbreaks. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h3)

question: At what point should healthcare waste segregation take place?

options.A: At the exact point of generation by the clinician
options.B: At the municipal dumping site by waste collectors
options.C: At the end of the shift in the utility room
options.D: After the waste has been compacted in the basement

explanation: Segregation must happen immediately at the point of generation to minimize handling risks and prevent errors. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of using puncture-resistant safety boxes?

options.A: To store confidential patient files securely
options.B: To collect general office stationery and paper
options.C: To safely contain needles, syringes, and sharp blades

explanation: Safety boxes are specifically designed to be puncture-resistant to prevent needlestick injuries from sharps like needles and blades. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the maximum capacity to which waste bags should be filled before sealing?
explanation: Waste bags and containers should be sealed at three-quarters (75%) capacity to prevent bursting, spilling, or accidental exposure. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: How should waste bags be lifted and carried during transport?

options.A: Clutched tightly against the chest for better balance
options.B: Dragged along the floor to reduce arm fatigue
options.C: Lifted by their necks away from the body
options.D: Balanced on the head for easy navigation

explanation: Bags must be lifted by their necks away from the body to protect against punctures from improperly discarded sharps hidden inside. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which waste treatment technology uses high-pressure steam to destroy all microbial life including spores?
explanation: Autoclaving uses pressurized steam and moist heat to effectively sterilize infectious waste and destroy microbial spores. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is a primary advantage of modern dual-chamber incineration?

options.A: It converts all plastic waste into reusable medical equipment
options.B: It operates at low temperatures without producing emissions
options.C: It completely destroys pathogens and anatomical waste while reducing volume
options.D: It requires no specialized operator training

explanation: Incineration uses high temperatures to achieve complete thermal destruction of pathogens and anatomical waste while significantly reducing waste volume. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the recommended immediate action following an accidental needlestick injury?

options.A: Apply an antiseptic ointment and bandage without washing
options.B: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out all trapped blood
options.C: Wash the site immediately with soap and running water
options.D: Ignore it if the patient appears healthy and asymptomatic

explanation: Washing the injured site immediately with soap and running water helps remove contaminants and reduces the risk of pathogen transmission. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h7)

question: Which vaccination is mandatory for nursing students and clinical staff to prevent occupational blood-borne infections?
explanation: Hepatitis B immunization is mandatory for healthcare workers to protect against occupational exposure to blood-borne pathogens. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h7)

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental standards and regulations, including medical waste management?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)
options.B: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA)
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)

explanation: NESREA is the key federal agency tasked with enforcing environmental standards and regulations enforcement across Nigerian facilities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h8)

question: What is a major challenge affecting medical waste management in some Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: An excess of advanced incinerators in rural clinics
options.B: Erratic electricity supply and infrastructural deficits

explanation: Infrastructural deficits and erratic power supply hinder the effective operation of waste treatment technologies like incinerators in Nigerian facilities. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h8)
